prompt: A robot moves on a grid from (0, 0) to (4, 3), each step going one unit right or one unit up. How many different routes are there?

options.explanation: 12 = 4 × 3 multiplies the dimensions. Routes are sequences of moves, not grid cells.
128 = 2⁷ treats each of the 7 steps as a free choice, but then most routes would not end at (4, 3).
Correct. Every route is 7 moves containing exactly 4 Rs and 3 Us. Choosing the 3 positions for the Us gives C(7, 3) = 35.
5,040 = 7! treats the 7 moves as all different. All Rs are the same, as are all Us: 7!/(4!·3!) = 35.

workedExample:
1. Any route makes exactly 4 right moves and 3 up moves: 7 moves.
2. A route is determined by which of the 7 positions are U.

```formula
N = C(7, 3) = (7 × 6 × 5) / 3!
N = 210 / 6 = 35
where
N: the number of routes from (0, 0) to (4, 3)
C(7, 3): "7 choose 3", the number of ways to choose which 3 of the 7 moves are up-moves
!: factorial: 3! = 3 × 2 × 1 = 6
In words: choosing the 3 up-move positions out of 7 fixes the whole route, so there are 35 routes.
```
